label: copy-phase outputs in length-3 sequences (plus a few fixed copy positions at L=4 and L=9)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), and only on repeated tokens (in_first=0); never in the original phase or on <DEL>. The core is length-3 sequences: it is active on about 73% of their two copy steps (t=4,5), most strongly at recall_idx 2 (the last output; 83% precision), and these hold about 47% of activation mass, including all of the top activations (e.g. c u z <DEL> c [u]). Outside L=3 it fires on a few fixed (L, recall_idx) positions, gated by token: L=4 recall 2 (15% rate, 14% mass), L=9 recall 3 (13% rate, 13% mass) and L=9 recall 8 (6%, 7.5% mass). It is almost never active for L=5, and only weakly for L=6-8. Within these positions it prefers input tokens g and i, but token gating does not give a clean rule. Adding those positions to the predicate raises mass recall to 0.81 but drops precision to 0.17, so the predicate covers only the L=3 core.
